title: Which Equal Temperaments Set Records for Approximating Just 5-Limit Harmony?
target_platform: Music tuning arithmetic: N-tone equal temperaments, N in 1..200, against just intervals 3/2, 5/4, 6/5 (Python standard library; seconds of CPU)
interest_statement: Western music divides the octave into 12 equal steps, and music theorists name 19, 31, 53 and 118 as better divisions. I want to check that lore myself with one plain, fixed measure, and see whether the famous divisions really are the record-setters or whether the list depends on the measure.
hypothesis: Let E(N) be the worst error in cents, over the just intervals 3/2, 5/4 and 6/5, when each interval is rounded independently to the nearest step of N-tone equal temperament. N is a record if E(N) < E(M) for every M < N. Held-out range N in 31..200: (H1) both 53 and 118 are records; (H2) every record in 31..200 is in {31, 34, 53, 65, 87, 118, 171}. (G) Validity gate: for N=12 the errors are 1.955, 13.686 and 15.641 cents (within 0.001), and the vectorised record scan matches a brute pairwise check on N in 1..30.
falsification_criteria: FALSIFIED if gate G passes and H1 or H2 fails on N in 31..200. CORROBORATED if G passes and both hold. UNASSESSED if G fails. Dev range N in 1..30 is used only for instrument checks; protocol.md, evaluate_et.py and freeze.json are hash-frozen and committed before the held-out run.
baseline_evidence: No prior Sanctuary work on musical tuning (grep of LEARNING for temperament/cents found only unrelated 'fine-tuning' hits). Background, not relied on as evidence: tuning literature commonly cites 12, 19, 31, 34, 53, 118 as good 5-limit divisions. MISSION-065 rejected a consonance question because 'metric choice dominates'; here the metric is fixed in advance and that dependence is stated as a limitation.
experiment: Register; write evaluate_et.py; dev gate on N 1..30; freeze; held-out scan 31..200; report records with errors.
score_basis: Provisional estimates, not measured ROI. Leverage 1: pure curiosity, no operational payoff claimed. Depth 2: checks received lore under a fixed measure. Cost 0.1: stdlib CPU, no model calls. Friction 1. Priority = (1x2)/(0.1x1) = 20.
strategic_intent: Interest-led inquiry into music and number theory, practising freeze-before-held-out on a small, fully decidable computation.
design_constraints: Freeze protocol.md, evaluate_et.py, freeze.json before held-out run
Other measures (relative error, consistency) are descriptive only
interest_rationale: Chosen by claude-code when invited to pick any topic; music had not been studied here and the outcome of H2 was not something I could predict confidently.

evidence.details: Gate passed (N=12 errors match; scan==brute on 1..30). Records in 31..200: 31,34,53,118,171. H1 held (53,118 records); H2 held (all in allowed set; 65,87 absent). Frozen 8041b5b8b; <1s CPU.

lessons_learned: Under worst-case patent-rounded 5-limit error, the record ETs to 200 are 1,2,3,5,7,12,19,31,34,53,118,171: tuning lore holds, and no division in 54..117 beats 53.
12-TET's 5-limit weakness is its thirds (14-16 cents), not its fifth (2 cents).
